2607.14905.title: Show Me How You Reason and I'll Tell You Who You Are: Reasoning Graphs for Robust LLM Authorship Attribution
2607.14905.paper_summary: Given the current trend to employ large language models (LLMs) in almost any imaginable context, LLM-generated text detection and authorship attribution have become a pressing issue. Prior work has primarily focused on surface-level linguistic features, an approach shown to be susceptible to paraphrasing and other obfuscation techniques. In this paper, we go beyond the linguistic surface, extracting and analysing reasoning structures in LLM-generated texts with the goal of capturing more complex signals of LLM authorship. We propose a graph neural network approach that leverages reasoning graphs extracted by an argument mining pipeline, demonstrating improved robustness and generalisation over a traditional Longformer baseline. Our approach outperforms the baseline by up to 27 percentage points under the obfuscation attacks such as paraphrasing and backtranslation, and 19 percentage points when evaluated on the texts generated by the unseen model versions, simulating real-world conditions in which new LLM versions are continuously released.
2607.14905.paper_summary_zh: 考慮到目前在幾乎任何可想像的情境中使用大型語言模型（LLMs）的趨勢，LLM生成的文本檢測和作者歸屬已成為一個緊迫的問題。先前的研究主要集中在表面層次的語言特徵上，這種方法已被證明容易受到改寫和其他混淆技術的影響。在本文中，我們超越語言表面，提取和分析LLM生成文本中的推理結構，目的是捕捉更複雜的LLM作者信號。我們提出了一種圖神經網絡方法，利用由論證挖掘管道提取的推理圖，展示出相較於傳統的Longformer基線更好的穩健性和泛化能力。在面對如改寫和回譯等混淆攻擊時，我們的方法在基線上提高了多達27個百分點的表現，而在評估未見模型版本生成的文本時則提高了19個百分點，模擬了新LLM版本不斷發布的真實世界條件。
